value.rationale: The example proves nonexistence of the precise Shapley-fair plus strict merge-stability equilibrium at the minimum possible number of players, despite every coalition having nonnegative value. It demonstrates a concrete failure mechanism in the purported convergence argument: strict beneficial mergers can increase negative Shapley mass, causing lexicographic descent. This has direct bearing on conditions needed for stable coalition-formation algorithms, rather than being a routine computation.
